# Creating packages with the wizard

This page is for developers and designers who build the parts of a site package in the browser. The package wizard
(**Setup > Packages > Create new package**, `/package/create`) exports classes, content, extensions or a site style
from a working installation into a new package. It is the easiest way to produce the packages your site package
requires; it does not produce the site package itself.

7x and the Exponential Foundation strongly encourage you to submit the finished site package by pull request to
se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth: see [Contribute your site package](../contribute-your-site-package.md).

## Contents

1. [What the wizard can make](#what-the-wizard-can-make)
2. [What it cannot make](#what-it-cannot-make)
3. [Making a package](#making-a-package)
4. [The information step](#the-information-step)
5. [From the wizard to your source repository](#from-the-wizard-to-your-source-repository)

## What the wizard can make

`package.ini [CreationSettings] HandlerList[]` names the creators; each makes one package type
(`kernel/classes/packagecreators/`):

| Wizard | Creator | Package type | Install type | Use in a site package |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Content class export | `ezcontentclass` | `contentclass` | install | your classes package, like `sevenx_classes` |
| Content object export | `ezcontentobject` | `contentobject` | install | your demo content package, like `sevenx_multisite_democontent` |
| Extension export | `ezextension` | `extension` | install | an extension shipped as a package |
| Site style | `ezstyle` | `sitestyle` | import | two stylesheets, images and a thumbnail |

The content object export can also be opened from the content tree (**Advanced > Export**), with the node and some
choices filled in: `/package/create/(creator)/ezcontentobject/(node)/<node id>`, optionally with `(subtree)/1`,
`(classes)/0|1` and `(versions)/current|all` (`kernel/package/module.php`).

## What it cannot make

None of the four creators writes a package of type `site`, and none writes `<settings>` or installer files. The site
package (its `package.xml` with `<type value="site" />`, its `<requires>` and its `settings/` folder) is made by
forking one ([Forking a site package](forking-a-site-package.md)) and edited by hand.

## Making a package

1. Open **Setup > Packages > Create new package**. Only the wizards your role may use are shown (`package/create`,
   limited by type, creator and role; see [Permissions for packages](../admin-gui/permissions-for-packages.md)).
2. Choose one and press **Start the wizard**.
3. Pick what goes in: classes in a table with a filter, nodes and subtrees through the content browser, extensions
   with their details. For content you also choose whether classes and templates go with it, which versions, which
   languages, and how node assignments and related objects are kept.
4. Fill in the package information, the maintainer (left out when your role may give no maintainer role) and the
   changelog.
5. Check the review on the last step and press **Create package**.

The step-by-step version with every field is
[The package creator wizard, step by step](../../designers/extensions/package-creator-wizard-step-by-step.md); the
redesigned wizard itself is described on [The package wizard](../../../features/6.0/package-wizard.md).

> **Note**
> The extension export is off until it is switched on: list the extension in `package.ini [ExtensionExportSettings]
> AllowedExtensions[]` (or `*`) and, with `RequirePolicy=enabled` (the default), grant `package/export_extension`. An
> extension that holds secret values or key material is refused either way
> ([The package secret check](../../designers/extensions/package-secret-check.md)).

## The information step

What the wizard checks before it goes on (`validatePackageInformation()` in `kernel/classes/ezpackagecreationhandler.php`):

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| Package name | required; "can only contain characters in the range a-z, 0-9 and underscore"; no package of that name may exist in any repository |
| Summary | required |
| Version | Semantic Versioning 2.0.0, `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` with optional `-prerelease` and `+build`, at most 24 characters; `1.0.0` is offered |
| License | one of `package.ini [LicenseSettings] LicenseList[]`; the default is `GPL-2.0-or-later` |
| Format | Classic XML (`package.xml`) or JSON (`package.json`) |

Choose the name the package will have in your index from the start: renaming later means editing `package.xml`, the
folder and every `<require>` that names it.

## From the wizard to your source repository

**Create package** writes the package into the `local` repository (`var/storage/packages/local/<name>/`) and opens its
page. To bring it into your source repository:

1. Press **Download** on the package's page: you get `<name>-<version>.ezpkg`.
2. Unpack it into `packages/<name>/` of your source repository and commit the files.
3. Set `<vendor>` in its `package.xml`: the wizard writes none, which is why the package sits in `local`; with a
   vendor, an import puts it in `var/storage/packages/<vendor>/`.
4. Name it in your site package's `<requires>` with a `min-version`, and list it in your `index.xml`.
5. Rebuild with `build.sh` like every other folder ([Rebuilding with build.sh](rebuilding-with-build-sh.md)).

> **Tip**
> Before you download, press **Validate** on the package's page: it checks the package as an upload would be
> checked, so a problem shows up on your test site and not on someone's new installation.
